tracks.legalName: Automatic Expunction of Dismissals and Findings of Not Guilty or Not Responsible under G.S. 15A-146(a4)
tracks.publicName: Your dismissed North Carolina case may have cleared itself
tracks.mechanism: Where a person is charged with a misdemeanor, a felony or an infraction and all charges in the case are disposed on or after December 1, 2021 by dismissal, a finding of not guilty, or a finding of not responsible, the charges are expunged by operation of law not less than 180 and not more than 210 days after the date of final disposition, if the statutory conditions are met. The General Assembly postponed the automatic process until July 1, 2024; it is now underway.
exclusions: Cases in which not every charge was disposed favorably.
Dismissals through deferred prosecution or conditional discharge, which are treated differently and route to the petition track.
Under G.S. 15A-146(a), no case with a felony charge dismissed pursuant to a plea agreement is expunged under that subsection.

Effective for dismissals on or after December 1, 2025, a dismissal by the court of a charge against a defendant found incapable to proceed is not eligible for expunction under G.S. 15A-146 and should not be included in an automatic expunction.

waitingPeriods.condition: All charges in the case disposed by dismissal, not guilty or not responsible on or after December 1, 2021
waitingPeriods.duration: Expunction occurs by operation of law not less than 180 and not more than 210 days after the date of final disposition

tracks.publicName: Ask an agency to clear a record that already cleared in court
tracks.mechanism: Where charges were expunged by operation of law under G.S. 15A-146(a4), the clerk is not required to transmit an expunction order to other entities. An agency that still holds and disseminates the charge may therefore be unaware the expunction occurred. G.S. 15A-153 restores the person to the status they occupied before the arrest, charge or conviction, and G.S. 15A-150 states the notification scheme for expunctions generally. This supporting action produces the participant's own written request asking the record holder to conform its records to the expunction that has already happened. It seeks no new relief and asks no court for anything.

Federal record holders and out-of-state agencies, which North Carolina expunction does not reach.
The court record itself, which is the clerk's and the AOC's to maintain under G.S. 15A-151(a1).

tracks.publicName: Your dismissed North Carolina case may have cleared itself
tracks.mechanism: Where a person is charged with a misdemeanor, a felony or an infraction and all charges in the case are disposed on or after December 1, 2021 by dismissal, a finding of not guilty, or a finding of not responsible, the charges are expunged by operation of law not less than 180 and not more than 210 days after the date of final disposition, if the statutory conditions are met. The General Assembly postponed the automatic process until July 1, 2024; it is now underway.

Under G.S. 15A-146(a), no case with a felony charge dismissed pursuant to a plea agreement is expunged under that subsection.

Effective for dismissals on or after December 1, 2025, a dismissal by the court of a charge against a defendant found incapable to proceed is not eligible for expunction under G.S. 15A-146 and should not be included in an automatic expunction.

tracks.legalName: Written Request to a Non-Court Record Holder to Conform Its Records to an Automatic Expunction under G.S. 15A-146(a4)
tracks.publicName: Ask an agency to clear a record that already cleared in court
tracks.mechanism: Where charges were expunged by operation of law under G.S. 15A-146(a4), the clerk is not required to transmit an expunction order to other entities. An agency that still holds and disseminates the charge may therefore be unaware the expunction occurred. G.S. 15A-153 restores the person to the status they occupied before the arrest, charge or conviction, and G.S. 15A-150 states the notification scheme for expunctions generally. This supporting action produces the participant's own written request asking the record holder to conform its records to the expunction that has already happened. It seeks no new relief and asks no court for anything.
exclusions: Any case where the automatic expunction under G.S. 15A-146(a4) has not in fact occurred. This action presupposes the expunction; where it did not run, the petition tracks apply instead.
Any case still inside the 180-to-210-day statutory window, which has not yet matured.
Federal record holders and out-of-state agencies, which North Carolina expunction does not reach.
The court record itself, which is the clerk's and the AOC's to maintain under G.S. 15A-151(a1).

destination.detail: Addressed to the agency the participant identifies from their own SBI criminal record check or from a background report. Nothing is filed with a court and no fee is paid. The letter states the case, the disposition, the disposition date, the statutory basis for the automatic expunction and the date the 210-day window closed, and asks the holder to conform its records. LegalEase writes the participant's request; it does not certify that the agency failed to act and does not assert that the expunction occurred as a matter of fact.

packetInstructions: The letter asks a record holder to conform its records to an expunction that has already happened.
